subject: Archaeology
title: Rock Art of the Sahara
description: A short lesson to help you apply Rock Art of the Sahara.

hook.text: The Sahara Desert is covered in rock art showing hippos, crocodiles, and cattle herders. It was once green.

buildup.text: Between 10,000 and 4,000 years ago, the Sahara had lakes, rivers, and grasslands supporting millions of people.

discovery.text: Tassili n'Ajjer in Algeria has over 15,000 engravings and paintings spanning 8,000 years of climate and culture.

twist.text: The art shows the transition from hunting to herding in real time. As the climate dried, animals in the art changed too.

climax.text: When the Sahara dried completely, people migrated to the Nile Valley — possibly seeding Egyptian civilization.

punchline.text: The Sahara recorded its own death in pictures.

quiz.question: What does Saharan rock art reveal about the region's past?
options: The Sahara was always a desert with nomadic populations
The region was once green with lakes, rivers, and millions of people
Ancient armies used the Sahara as a battlefield

details.summary: The Sahara Desert contains thousands of rock art images dating from 12,000 to 2,000 years ago, depicting a lush green landscape with rivers, cattle herds, giraffes, and swimming humans. This art documents the dramatic climate change that transformed North Africa from savanna to desert.
details.whyItMatters: Saharan rock art is a visual record of climate change. It shows that today's harshest desert was recently a fertile landscape, reminding us how dramatically environments can shift over relatively short timescales.
takeaways: Saharan rock art spans 12,000 to 2,000 years ago
It depicts a lush green landscape with rivers and wildlife
The art documents the transformation from savanna to desert

faq.question: Was the Sahara really green?
faq.answer: Yes. During the African Humid Period roughly 11,000 to 5,000 years ago, the Sahara had lakes, rivers, and grasslands supporting hippos, crocodiles, and large human populations. Orbital changes in Earth's tilt brought monsoon rains to regions that are now hyperarid desert.

faq.question: Where is the best Saharan rock art found?
faq.answer: The Tassili n'Ajjer plateau in Algeria contains over 15,000 images and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Other major concentrations exist in Libya's Acacus Mountains, Chad's Ennedi Plateau, and Egypt's Western Desert. Each region has distinct styles and chronologies.
